body: Added `emitting` property. I wanted to add this on a further update, but i tried making a VFX without it and it was not good at all.

Thanks a lot @Calinou for the thorough review!

> Personally, I would prefer if it was named Line3D to match Line2D naming, but I understand why a different name is used.

Yeah same! The rationale behind calling it ribbon 3D is the following
- It's unclear what exactly are the usecase for line3d other than trails
- This class is meant to draw a flat mesh, not a solid mesh, that's why it's called ribbon.
- If it was called Line3D, it should mimick the functionality of Line2D, for consistency and usability reasons
Given the above, I decided to take distance from Line3D and focus only on the tool for VFX.

I think a good middle ground could be to reserve the class Line3D, even if emtpy, so that if one day we want to add line3d, we can and we don't introduce different inheritance between Line2D and Line3D (especially considering there's an open PR for Trail2D).


> Is it planned to add a Texture property? There are properties to set the tiling mode, multiplier and UV pinning, so one could logically expect to be able to use a texture on the default materials.

I didn't plan to add a texture property for this, no. The rationale behind this is that any ribbon for VFX will need a custom shader, so there's no point in complicating the built-in one. I can be convinced otherwise though.

> The default material could have a property to fade trails and beams that are nearly perpendicular to the camera, to avoid obvious rotation:

Same as above, it's left to the user.

> Overbright/HDR colors can't be used in the gradient curve (they will be clamped). Perhaps something like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97604 is needed for Ribbon in the long run. (I assume it relies on vertex colors for the coloring, which can't be overbright in 4.x, as opposed to a texture.)

Is there no way to enable unclamped vertex colors? Seems like a big limitation.

> It's unclear what exactly are the usecase for line3d other than trails

Ropes, lasers, trajectory lines, debug visualization, just to name a few. For example Blender Studio's DOGWALK used the CozyCube's implementation for the leash.
If a Line3D was added it should be a more or less minimal node without trail functionality.

One thing I'd like to bring up is tube/cylinder trails (which I assume are out of scope here). Would that be a separate node or a mode in Ribbon3D (which should just be called Trail3D if it had non-ribbon modes imo)? If it would be a separate node then I think they should be called RibbonTrail3D and TubeTrail3D because just Tube3D sounds extremely vague (also I think I prefer RibbonTrail3D in general) (maybe they could both inherit from a single Trail3D base class if so?).

> Ropes, lasers, trajectory lines, debug visualization, just to name a few

This class does already the laser (just called beam instead of laser).

For debug visualization, there's no consensus on how that should be done. A lot of people don't want to use a node for it.
There's a lot of contradicting needs and a design needs to be sorted out first.

It's unclear to me whether ropes should be solid tubes or flat geometry. I haven't seen enough request/usecase to make a choice therefore I've built no tech for it.

> One thing I'd like to bring up is tube/cylinder trails (which I assume are out of scope here).

I don't have plans for those atm. On the contrary, solid geometry os something that I want to specifically leave out of the node made for VFX. Most VFX use flat geometry for trails. For pipes and static stuff we already have CSG.

> This class does already the laser (just called beam instead of laser).

I meant something like a laser that bounces off of surfaces, though you can probably bundle that with trajectory lines since it's a similar concept.

> It's unclear to me whether ropes should be solid tubes or flat geometry. I haven't seen enough request/usecase to make a choice therefore I've built no tech for it.
> I don't have plans for those atm. On the contrary, solid geometry is something that I want to specifically leave out of the node made for VFX. Most VFX use flat geometry for trails.

For both of these to me seem like a matter of size. For example if I wanted a trail the size of the player character that follows them, it would be very obvious if it was a flat billboard so I would rather use a tube.
For ropes if they're thin to me it seems more optimal to use flat geometry with a normal map to simulate cylindrical shading, but bigger ropes would likely need to be tubes (unless they are like background elements).

> For example if I wanted a trail the size of the player character that follows them, it would be very obvious if it was a flat billboard so I would rather use a tube.

The technique in those cases is a ribbon + skinned mesh emitter for particles + vertex shader on the character. I don't think a tube would solve the issue.

Just some musings during the rendering meeting, in general looks good.

We were wondering if there was a better approach then uploading a new mesh for the ribbon to the GPU. I guess it would be difficult because a different approach would be needed on OpenGL v.s. the RD renderer, but updating the ribbon GPU side would be more efficient.

The other point raised was wondering whether it really is more performant to update the mesh instead of just creating a new mesh and discarding the old. This would remove a bunch of complexity in how the mesh data is prepared and allows the driver to better optimise pushing the new data to the GPU.

Thank you @BastiaanOlij for reviewing the PR!

Yeah this is significantly faster (3-4x). Creating the mesh format every frame is pretty expensive, that's what I had done initially.

I think we can have GPU ribbons for Rd as a switch, but we should first evaluate demand for large number of trails and weight it against particle trails.

My open question for this PR is whether we want to commit to have trail3d not inherit from line3d. There is demand for line3d. My fallback solution is that we can later extract line3d as a mesh class rather than a node derivative, not sure yet of how feasible this is (open question is how to update it only once every frame and not give people a performance footgun by updating the mesh every time points are assigned)

I already notified @QbieShay of this separately, but uploading it here just for consolidation. There are a few glitches I found. Pretty easy to replicate in the sense that it's quite likely to happen within the span of a minute of playing around. But quite difficult to replicate in that I can't really find a rhyme or reason for a consistent repo.

Sometimes the trail just doesn't show up at all. Sometimes it dies too slowly. Sometimes it stops dying and remains in limbo.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27ef41c7-d592-48bb-affa-00df94b8a1b6

Performance got a lot better with the recent changes but there's still room for more.

The main issue right now is the entire vertex/index buffer getting uploaded and used in the GPU draw call, even if the actual frame had less points to draw. This is unnecessary work for no reason. 

Maybe a RS function could be added to set the vertex/index counts of a mesh surface after creation to avoid this.

I don't know if there's much that can be done about z-fighting in those situations. You can try changing the way pivots are calculated under the sorting tab, but in general those are 3d meshes that move and change every frame. This is an alpha sorting issue
